Our Values
Pupils enjoy their time in this inclusive and welcoming school. Each morning, they arrive confident, resilient and eager to learn. Forging positive relationships is at the heart of daily life. Pupils feel sure that staff care about them. This helps them to feel safe.
Ofsted Report, November 2025
The curriculum is ambitious, broad and balanced. It is carefully arranged so that pupils gainthe knowledge and skills needed for their next stage of education. Leaders have a secure understanding of the quality of teaching and learning. They act quickly when improvements are required and show determination to keep raising standards.
Ofsted Report, November 2025

pageCache.pageTitle: Dunmore Primary School - Personal, Social, Health & Economic Eduction (PSHE)
pageCache.text:
Personal, Social, Health & Economic Eduction (PSHE)
Dunmore holds children at its heart, and our vision for PSHE helps children understand and value how they fit into and contribute to the world, with strong emphasis on emotional literacy, building resilience and nurturing mental and physical health. We use Jigsaw PSHE plans to deliver engaging and relevant PSHE within a whole-school approach. Lessons include mindfulness allowing children to advance their emotional awareness, concentration, focus and self-regulation.
PSHE Jigsaw Curriculum Overview

Maths
The teaching of Maths at Dunmore is underpinned by the belief that Maths should inspire, include and challenge children, within a curriculum based on fluency and mastery. Children are given the opportunity to build strong foundations with secure knowledge of the four operations (+-X/) alongside understanding of mathematical concepts involving measures, fractions, geometry and algebra. We use manipulatives and models to strengthen these foundations and develop conceptual understanding. Children are encouraged to use appropriate mathematical language and have regular opportunities to solve challenging problems. We strive to ensure that every child becomes a confident mathematician with a sense of enjoyment and curiosity about the subject.
We are following the White Rose Maths (WRM) Scheme of Learning. We use many of the White Rose resources, supplemented with resources from other providers. We have adopted the WRM calculation policy.
Maths Resources for Parents
For further information on how you can help your child with maths, we recommend the parent hub on White Rose Maths website https://whiteroseeducation.com/parent-pupil-resources/maths
The WRM website has some excellent resources, including videos and parent guides:
https://whiteroseeducation.com/parent-pupil-resources/maths/maths-with-michael#watch
The free 1-Minute Maths app from WRM is also fantastic for practising fundamental number skills:
We also use Times Tables Rock Stars, which we set as maths homework and play in school. Your child will get a log in during year 1, and will use TTRS all the way to the end of year 6.
If you want to do some extra maths at home with your child, the White Rose Power Maths Practice Books (Year A, B and C - one for each long term) follow our curriculum. They are available through online stores including here.
Dunmore Maths Vocabulary Progression
Maths Yearly Overview

Music
Music is sequenced and tailored through high quality lessons equipping all children with the knowledge and skills needed to make and to appreciate good music. By providing opportunities to engage in singing, playing, composing and listening, we hope to give all children a sense of achievement and to inspire them to develop a life-long love of music.
Dunmore Music Curriculum
Dunmore Music Development Plan Dunmore 2025-2026

pageCache.pageTitle: Dunmore Primary School - Parents and Carers of Children with SEND
pageCache.text:
Parents and Carers of Children with SEND
We are committed to working with parents and carers to identify their child’s needs and support. Parents and carers will be involved throughout the process.
There is a range of ways this can be done. For example:
Regular SEND Coffee Mornings
Parents/ carers evenings;
Questionnaires
Gold Book weekly awards

Art
Through Art at Dunmore, we introduce children to the joys of learning via visual means. We believe that creativity is in us all and everyone has the right to express themselves, without barriers. Through our creative climate, we strive for excellence, providing ideas, inspiration and teaching techniques to enable children to explore a wide variety of media. We seek opportunities to collaborate with artists, galleries and museums and enrich other areas of our Curriculum with our Art exploration. The beauty of ‘Art’ is in the eye of the beholder and at Dunmore we recognise and celebrate this diversity.
Dunmore Art Curriculum

Computing
Welcome to Computing!
At Dunmore, we believe that every child is a digital innovator! Our computing curriculum ignites curiosity and empowers pupils to become confident and creative users of technology. We aim to equip them with the essential skills and knowledge to navigate the digital world safely and responsibly.
Through engaging and hands-on experiences, children will learn the fundamentals of computer science, from coding and algorithms to understanding how technology works. We foster critical thinking, problem-solving, and collaboration, preparing them for future success in an increasingly digital society. Our intent is to inspire a lifelong love of learning and to empower our pupils to use technology to shape a better future.
Dunmore Computing Curriculum

English
The English curriculum at Dunmore is underpinned by a love of language and stories, and their ability to open new worlds for children. We have selected a diverse range of rich texts to drive our English learning journeys. At the start of each unit of work, children explore a text in detail using class discussions, detailed vocabulary work, drama and more. Writing outcomes are clearly modelled to inspire and support children, and key grammar, punctuation and spelling skills are taught in context before students put these into practice in their own written work. We encourage all children to strive for excellence in their spoken and written English (including handwriting), enabling them to communicate their ideas clearly and effectively. Comprehension skills are taught through daily guided reading sessions, where children encounter additional rich texts, chosen to suit their ability and capture their imaginations.
Recommended books, by year group
We love reading in school. If you would like some book ideas for age-appropriate stories at home, here are 50 recommended texts by year group:
Handwriting
We follow the Debbie Hepplewhite handwriting programme.
Dunmore English Curriculum
Handwriting poster

French
At Dunmore Primary School, our teaching of French is supported using the resources from the ‘French with Mr Innes’ programme https://frenchwithmrinnes.com/. This programme supports the National Curriculum’s Foreign Language expectations in Key Stage 2. The programme has a holistic approach to support the attainment of the National Curriculum aims. As such, each aim is progressively attained by learners over the course of the four-year programme. In line with the National Curriculum values, French with Mr Innes focuses on practical communication, with a fun and authentic approach through videos based in Paris, flashcards, worksheets, games and challenges. The programme seeks to equip KS2 pupils to be ready for further French learning in KS3. Over the course of French with Mr Innes, learners will be able understand and communicate ideas, facts and feelings in speech and writing through their knowledge of phonics, grammar and vocabulary.
Dunmore French Curriculum

Geography
Welcome to Geography!
Geography at Dunmore provides pupils with a range of opportunities to explore and understand the world in which we live and its people. We use our local surroundings in Abingdon, as well as Oxfordshire and the South of England, to give children practical experiences of both human and physical geography. Our curriculum is taught through termly topics designed to give all children a life-long curiosity to discover more about our planet. Teachers create meaningful cross-curricular links, while also making it explicit to children that they are learning key geographical knowledge and skills. This helps to provoke questions and provide answers about the natural and human aspects of the world.
Children are encouraged to develop a greater understanding and knowledge of the world, as well as their place in it. Geography is an investigative subject, which develops an understanding of concepts, knowledge, and skills. At Dunmore, we aim to inspire a curiosity and fascination about the world and people within it; to promote the children’s interest and understanding of diverse places, people, resources and natural and human environments, together with a deep understanding of the Earth’s key physical and human processes.
Dunmore Geography Curriculum

History
The History curriculum at Dunmore inspires and challenges children to become curious and critical thinkers, developing the skills needed to become historians. Learning is underpinned by a chronological narrative, enabling children to understand people’s lives, changes over time and the diversity of societies. Through studying history of the wider world, incorporating evidence from our local area of Abingdon and Oxford, children develop an understanding of their own identities and history.
Dunmore History Curriculum

Physical Education
Welcome to Physical Education!
The Physical Education we deliver at Dunmore and the enjoyment of it aims to establish attitudes towards exercise and a healthy lifestyle that will be adopted by each pupil throughout their life. We follow recommendations from the Chief Medical Officer to provide 30 minutes of activity every day along with two hours of high-quality Physical Education every week. This is delivered through a wide range of quality sports and experiences including Paralympic sports.
Dunmore PE Curriculum

pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
At Dunmore Primary School, we recognise that all pupils are entitled to a quality of provision that will enable them to achieve their potential. We believe in positive intervention, removing barriers to learning, raising expectations and levels of achievement, and working in partnership with other agencies to provide a positive educational experience for all of our pupils, including those with special educational needs or disabilities (SEND).
Our school recognises that there are groups of pupils whose circumstances require additional consideration by those who work with them to support their SEND.
Our Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Co-Ordinator is Mrs Sarah Smith. Mrs Smith's priorities are to ensure that all pupils, regardless of their specific needs, make the best possible progress.
This SEND Information Report should be read alongside the school’s SEND Policy, the Equalities Information and Objectives and the Accessibility Plan, which can be found in the School Policies section.
SEN Information Report September 2025
Mr Sam Bartholomew - Headteacher (head.3861@dunmore.oxon.sch.uk)

Mrs Nicky Black - SEND Governor (nblack@dunmore.oxon.sch.uk)
Mrs Pina Ross – Assistant Headteacher and Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) (pros3517@dunmore.oxon.sch.uk)
Mrs Anne Platt - Family Liaison Officer (flo@dunmore.oxon.sch.uk)
At Dunmore Primary School we aim to provide an inclusive and broad curriculum which inspires and challenges all children within a safe, secure and stimulating learning environment.
The SEND policy is available on the Policies page.
Family Information Directory (oxfordshire.gov.uk)

SEND Admissions
For information on the admission of pupils with a disability, please visit the Local Authority Admissions policy and view the Accessibility Plan in our School Policies section. If you would like to discuss your child’s SEND in more detail, please contact the school to arrange an appointment.
The full range of local support available for children/ young people with SEND and their families within and outside of school can be found in the Oxfordshire Local Offer:
Special educational needs and disability: The local offer | Oxfordshire County Council

Design & Technology
Welcome to Design & Technology!
Design and Technology at Dunmore provides children with a real-life context for learning. We want to allow children to aspire to achieve more by creating opportunities for them in the wider world. Through the DT curriculum, children should be inspired by engineers, designers, chefs and architects to enable them to create a range of structures, mechanisms, textiles and food products with a real-life purpose.
Dunmore DT Curriculum
